# MCP Tool Index

All 84 tools that `quipu mcp` and `quipu-server` serve in a build with the `owl` feature, generated from the tool definitions. For connection details, workflows and examples see [MCP Tools](mcp-tools.md).

## `quipu_accept_proposal`

Accept a pending schema proposal. For shape proposals, validates the Turtle before writing to the shapes table. A proposal carrying a migration runs it in the same transaction; a refused migration leaves the proposal pending and nothing written. With dry_run=true nothing is accepted: the report lists existing facts the new shapes would refuse, what the migration would change, and whether acceptance would go through. Before accepting, a blast-radius plan is computed and returned as 'plan'; a plan whose risk score exceeds risk_threshold, or that cannot be determined, is refused unless accept_risk=true with a risk_reason (recorded in the decision note).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accept_risk` | boolean | no | Accept a failing or undetermined plan anyway; requires risk_reason |
| `decided_by` | string | yes | Identity of the approver (required; there is no default) |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Report what acceptance would do without accepting (default false) |
| `id` | integer | yes | Proposal ID to accept |
| `limit` | integer | no | Dry run: maximum sample facts and violations per list (default 50, max 1000) |
| `note` | string | no | Optional acceptance note |
| `risk_reason` | string | no | Why the risk is accepted; recorded in the decision note |
| `risk_threshold` | integer | no | Refuse when the plan's risk score is above this (0-100; default 40 or QUIPU_PROPOSAL_RISK_THRESHOLD) |
| `timestamp` | string | no | ISO-8601 timestamp |

## `quipu_align_apply`

WRITE. Materialise decided alignments as owl:sameAs / quipu:distinctFrom in a derived alignment graph. expected_version is REQUIRED and must be carried from the decision: computing it here would hash the set being written, always match, and silently discard a concurrent operator's decision.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is applying. |
| `expected_version` | string | yes | REQUIRED. From align_propose or align_decide. Never recomputed locally. |
| `graph_a` | string | yes | First source graph IRI (the pair given to align_propose). |
| `graph_b` | string | yes | Second source graph IRI. |
| `set_tsv` | string | yes | Decided SSSOM TSV from align_decide. |

## `quipu_align_decide`

READ. Apply operator accept/negate decisions to a proposed mapping set. Touches no store. Returns the decided set and the expected_version to carry into align_apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `decisions` | array | yes | Per-pair verdicts. |
| `reviewer` | string | yes | Who is deciding. |
| `set_tsv` | string | yes | SSSOM TSV from align_propose. |

## `quipu_align_propose`

READ. Propose candidate cross-graph alignments between two named graphs, scored, as an SSSOM mapping set. Returns expected_version, which align_apply requires. Refuses an unknown graph IRI rather than returning 0 candidates.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `graph_a` | string | yes | First named-graph IRI. Must exist; an unknown IRI is refused, not treated as empty. |
| `graph_b` | string | yes | Second named-graph IRI. |
| `mapping_set_id` | string | no | Identifier for the produced mapping set. |

## `quipu_ask`

Run a curated, parameterized named query by name instead of hand-writing SPARQL. Call with no 'name' (or name='list') to discover the self-describing catalog of available queries and their parameters (e.g. service_deps, references_to, entity_facts, entities_of_type, labeled_like).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `graph` | string | no | Named graph override for the stored query. |
| `name` | string | no | Named query to run; omit (or 'list') to list the catalog. |
| `params` | object | no | Parameter map for the named query (see catalog for names/types). |

## `quipu_context`

Query the knowledge graph for context around a natural-language query: returns relevant entities and their facts, ready to prime an agent. Optionally expand to linked entities.

## `quipu_cooccurrence`

Deterministic, auditable work-item co-occurrence: given a work-item (Bead) IRI, returns the other work-items that share at least one touched code entity via the provenance chain Bead <-implements- GitCommit -modifies-> entity. A graph query over typed provenance edges, not a statistical mine; ordered by overlap strength. Bitemporal: pass valid_at for 'which work co-occurred as of <date>'.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tx` | integer | no | Maximum transaction ID to consider |
| `valid_at` | string | no | Point-in-time for valid-time filtering (ISO-8601) |
| `work_item` | string | yes | Work-item (Bead) IRI |

## `quipu_datasets`

Manage named datasets — a reusable NAME for an arbitrary set of graphs, so it can be labelled, governed and handed to another agent. `FROM <dataset-iri>` then means FROM over its members. Datasets overlap freely and are never implicitly active.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string: `create`, `list`, `show`, `remove` | no | Action to perform (default: list) |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is creating the dataset |
| `members` | array | no | Graph IRIs, or {"graph": "&lt;iri>", "ord": N} objects for a declared ordering. Duplicate ranks are refused. |
| `name` | string | no | Dataset IRI (required for create/show/remove) |
| `timestamp` | string | no | ISO-8601 timestamp |

## `quipu_explain`

Walk a fact's derivation chain: a base fact answers with its transaction and source; a reasoner:<rule-id> fact answers with the rule and the premises it currently re-matches; an owl:materialize fact answers with every axiom family that currently re-derives it, premises recursed to base facts. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `depth` | integer | no | Recursion depth for the derivation walk (default: 5) |
| `o` | string | yes | Object IRI, or a string literal |
| `p` | string | yes | Predicate IRI |
| `s` | string | yes | Subject IRI |

Export deterministic RDF scoped to one named graph, provenance group, SPARQL CONSTRUCT, or ROOT when no scope is supplied. Scope fields are mutually exclusive.

| `graph` | string | no | Named-graph IRI to export. Omit for the ROOT/default graph. Unknown IRI is an error. |

## `quipu_graph`

Project the knowledge graph into a render-ready node-link payload in ONE response: nodes (iri, label, rdf:type, degree), edges as [source_index, target_index, predicate] into that node array, and a type census ordered by prevalence. Excludes prov:Activity episodes and rdf/rdfs/prov scaffolding predicates by default so the domain graph is not buried in provenance. Nodes are ranked by degree and capped; the response states what was dropped.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edge_budget` | integer | no | Maximum number of projected edges. |
| `include_episodes` | boolean | no | Include prov:Activity episode nodes (default: false) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Max nodes to return, ranked by degree (default: 250, hard max: 2000) |
| `type` | string | no | Restrict to nodes of this rdf:type IRI (edges are scoped to the filtered set too) |

## `quipu_graph_freeze`

Deep-freeze a named graph: export its FULL history (retracted rows and transactions included) into a read-only archive pack, verify the copy by content hash, delete the local rows, and re-attach the pack so the graph stays addressable at the same IRI. Compose frozen graphs back in with FROM <iri>, the urn:quipu:dataset:frozen dataset, or include_kinds:["archive"]. Refuses ROOT, the meta-graph, overlays, attached graphs, and double-freezes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is freezing |
| `graph` | string | yes | IRI of the committed graph to freeze |
| `out_dir` | string | no | Directory for the archive pack (default: beside the store file) |
| `timestamp` | string | yes | ISO-8601 timestamp |

## `quipu_graph_list`

List registered named graphs; optional graph selects one exact registered IRI without materialization enrichment (cannot combine with kind/lifecycle). Includes class, source, lifecycle and labels (freshness/durability/trust/policy/kind). Filter with `kind` (a dataKind token, e.g. operational | archive) and/or `lifecycle` (frozen). Also the capability probe for the graph-kinds surface: a store without this tool predates it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `graph` | string | no | Exact registered graph IRI; no kind/lifecycle combination or materialization enrichment |
| `kind` | string | no | Only graphs declaring this dataKind token |
| `lifecycle` | string: `frozen` | no | Only graphs in this storage lifecycle state |

## `quipu_graph_thaw`

Thaw a frozen graph: verify its archive pack, detach it, restore the full history into the local store under the same IRI, and reopen the graph for writes. The pack file is kept on disk; the freeze registry row is closed, never deleted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is thawing |
| `graph` | string | yes | IRI of the frozen graph |
| `timestamp` | string | yes | ISO-8601 timestamp |

## `quipu_health`

Read server health as a positive liveness control; healthy does not prove complete graph coverage.

No parameters.

## `quipu_hybrid_search`

Combined SPARQL + vector similarity search with predicate pushdown. Accepts a pre-computed embedding or natural-language query. Simple type constraints (e.g. ?s a <Type>) are pushed into the vector index for O(log n) filtered ANN.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `embedding` | array | no | Pre-computed query embedding vector (f32 array). Takes precedence over query. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum results (default: 10) |
| `query` | string | no | Natural language search query (auto-embedded when EmbeddingProvider is attached) |
| `sparql` | string | no | SPARQL SELECT query returning entity IRIs in the first variable. Simple type patterns (e.g. ?s a &lt;Type>) enable predicate pushdown. |
| `valid_at` | string | no | Point-in-time for temporal filtering (ISO-8601) |

## `quipu_impact`

Impact analysis: walk downstream from an entity. With remove=true, speculatively retracts the entity first (counterfactual: 'what would break if I removed this?'). The store is never mutated.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | string | yes | IRI of the entity to analyse |
| `hops` | integer | no | Maximum edge hops to follow (default: 5) |
| `predicates` | array | no | Restrict walk to these predicate IRIs. Empty = all edges. |
| `rank_by_ppr` | boolean | no | Order the reached set by Personalized PageRank seeded at the root (each entry gains a 'ppr' score) instead of BFS discovery order (default: false) |
| `remove` | boolean | no | If true, speculatively retract the entity before walking (counterfactual mode). Default: false. |
| `timestamp` | string | no | ISO-8601 timestamp for the speculative retraction (used only when remove=true) |

## `quipu_import_promote`

Promote a staged share only when existing promotion gates permit it. Does not bypass quarantine or resolution review. With target_graph, promote into that named graph instead of ROOT, replacing only the share's subjects there; with retire_from too, move those subjects out of that source graph in the same transaction. With dry_run, report what the move would assert, replace and retire, and write nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no |  |
| `retire_from` | string | no |  |
| `share_id` | string | yes |  |
| `target_graph` | string | no |  |

## `quipu_knot`

Assert facts into the knowledge graph (with optional SHACL validation)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is making the assertion |
| `blank_node_scope` | string | no | Explicit document scope: distinct IDs separate identical loads; the same ID shares nodes across graphs only for identical input bytes. |
| `graph` | string | no | Named-graph IRI to write into. Must already be registered committed-class (graph_create). Unknown IRI is an error, never interned. Omit for ROOT. |
| `replace_snapshot` | boolean | no | Replace the prior facts written under this snapshot key (diffed: unchanged facts stay live). Requires 'snapshot'. |
| `shapes` | string | no | Optional SHACL shapes in Turtle for validation |
| `snapshot` | string | no | Stable producer key (e.g. 'bobbin-chunks:myrepo'). Facts written with it, with or without replace_snapshot, are owned by source 'snapshot:&lt;key>' and a later replace under the same key retracts them; 'source' is then ignored. Scoped to the target graph. |
| `source` | string | no | Provenance source (episode, file, etc.) |
| `timestamp` | string | no | TRANSACTION time: when this store came to believe the facts. Defaults to now. Also the valid-time unless valid_from is given. |
| `turtle` | string | yes | RDF data in Turtle format to assert |
| `valid_from` | string | no | VALID time: when the facts became true OF THE WORLD, independent of when they were ingested. RFC 3339; a UTC offset (e.g. git's 2026-09-07T07:19:41+02:00) is normalised to Z and sub-second precision is dropped, because valid-time is compared as text. Malformed values are refused before anything is written. Omit to reuse timestamp — the absent case is byte-identical to the old behaviour. |

## `quipu_merge_apply`

WRITE. Finish a share merge (incoming + base) or a fork promotion (fork): the clean part plus every decided row in ONE transaction whose source records the reviewer and the decisions hash. Refuses and writes nothing on an undecided row, stale decisions (either side moved), more values than sh:maxCount, a value that is not an RDF term, or (forks) a SHACL refusal. Applying the same decisions again returns outcome already-applied and writes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is applying. |
| `base` | object | no | Its parent share. Inline, as /import takes it. |
| `decisions` | object | yes | The file from merge_decisions with each row's decision set (quipu_merge_resolve): {choose: ours\|theirs\|base\|both} or {values: [N-Triples terms]}. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Run every check and report the counts it would write; write nothing. |
| `fork` | string | no | Apply to this fork's promotion, instead of incoming + base. |
| `incoming` | object | no | The share to merge. Inline, as /import takes it. |
| `reviewer` | string | yes | Who decided. Recorded in provenance. |

## `quipu_merge_decisions`

READ. The conflicts of merging an incoming share (incoming + base) or promoting a fork (fork) into ROOT, one row per slot with base/ours/theirs values and each side's provenance, bound to what was reviewed. propose:true adds a mechanical proposal with evidence per row; it never sets a decision. present:true returns {decisions, presentation, view}: the standard markdown to show the user, unchanged. Writes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | object | no | Its parent share. Inline, as /import takes it. |
| `fork` | string | no | A fork whose promotion stopped on conflicts, instead of incoming + base. |

## `quipu_path_backtest`

Golden paths: backtest a pruned candidate (exemplar trajectory minus omitted steps) over recorded history — which past trajectories with a shared work-item topic would have conformed under gp-grammar/1, and how did their work items close? Distinguishes 0 matches from cannot-evaluate, and refuses a pattern it cannot compile.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base_ns` | string | no | Vocabulary namespace override; defaults to the store's configured base_ns. |
| `exemplar` | string | yes | IRI of the exemplar Trajectory |
| `omit` | array | no | Step IRIs the candidate omits |

## `quipu_path_cone`

Golden paths: compute the provenance cone of a trajectory — which steps did its falsifier-gated verified result depend on? Per-step verdicts are in-cone (load-bearing; pruning needs a human Decision), out-of-cone (mechanically prunable), or cannot-evaluate (no derivation edges recorded — never silently prunable). Refuses trajectories with no steps or no falsifier-gated verification.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base_ns` | string | no | Vocabulary namespace override; defaults to the store's configured base_ns. |
| `hops` | integer | no | Depth bound for the derivation walk (default: 8) |
| `trajectory` | string | yes | IRI of the Trajectory to analyse |
| `via` | array | no | Derivation predicate IRIs to walk, in addition to verifiedBy (always followed). |

## `quipu_policy_check`

Committed-tier evaluation of a governance Policy over the graph of record: evaluates the policy's aegis:claim (a SPARQL ASK, optionally with a $target placeholder) against the committed graph and returns a Verdict — outcome ∈ {satisfied | unsatisfied | unknown} bound to a reproducible evidence_hash. Deterministic and reproducible: any verifier re-running the same ASK over the same committed evidence gets the same verdict (checked, not trusted). Returns the verdict UNSIGNED (signing + persistence is the Phase-0 verifier registry's job).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claim` | string | no | Inline SPARQL ASK claim (alternative to 'policy') |
| `evidence_probe` | string | no | Inline ASK for 'does the evidence exist?' — false yields outcome 'unknown' instead of 'unsatisfied' |
| `policy` | string | no | Policy IRI whose aegis:claim to evaluate (alternative to inline 'claim') |
| `predicate_id` | string | no | Predicate identifier recorded in the verdict (inline claims only; default: 'inline') |
| `target` | string | yes | Target IRI bound to the $target placeholder |
| `tx` | integer | no | Maximum transaction for the policy evaluation. |
| `valid_at` | string | no | Point-in-time for valid-time evaluation (ISO-8601). Omit for current state. |

## `quipu_project`

Project the knowledge graph and run a graph algorithm over it: stats (node/edge counts), in_degree (most-referenced entities), pagerank/ppr (global or personalized PageRank from seed entities), components (weakly-connected components), louvain (modularity community detection), or shortest_path. Optionally restrict the projection to a node type or predicate. Read-only by default; louvain with persist:true writes quipu:memberOfCommunity facts (superseding any prior derivation).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `algorithm` | string: `stats`, `in_degree`, `pagerank`, `ppr`, `components`, `louvain`, `shortest_path` | no | Algorithm to run (default: stats) |
| `damping` | number | no | PageRank damping factor (default: 0.85) |
| `from` | string | no | Source entity IRI for shortest_path |
| `graph` | string | no | Project ONE named graph's own facts instead of ROOT (quipu-tz5) — cheap against a small derived layer even when the episode log is large |
| `limit` | integer | no | Max results for in_degree/pagerank (default: 20) |
| `max_iters` | integer | no | PageRank max iterations (default: 100) |
| `persist` | boolean | no | louvain only: persist quipu:memberOfCommunity facts (emergent clustering, NOT an access boundary), bitemporally superseding any prior derivation (default: false) |
| `predicate` | string | no | Restrict the projection to edges with this predicate IRI |
| `seeds` | array | no | Seed entity IRIs (or raw term IDs) for personalized PageRank; non-empty switches pagerank to PPR |
| `timestamp` | string | no | Timestamp used for persisted community assignments. |
| `to` | string | no | Target entity IRI for shortest_path |
| `tolerance` | number | no | PageRank convergence tolerance (default: 1e-6) |
| `type` | string | no | Restrict the projection to nodes of this rdf:type IRI |

## `quipu_retract`

Retract ROOT/default-graph facts for an entity: all of them, or narrowed by predicate and/or value. Supplying a graph field is refused; named-graph facts are untouched. Entity + predicate + value retracts exactly ONE (e,a,v) statement — use this to remove a stray edge instead of retracting a whole episode and rebuilding it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is performing the retraction |
| `allow_orphan` | boolean | no | Allow identity facts to be removed from a still-referenced entity. |
| `entity` | string | yes | IRI of the entity to retract |
| `graph` | any | no | Unsupported: omit this field. This tool operates only on ROOT/default graph; use graph-scoped quipu_update for named graphs. |
| `predicate` | string | no | Optional: only retract facts with this predicate IRI |
| `source` | string | no | Provenance source of the retraction. |
| `timestamp` | string | no | ISO-8601 timestamp for the retraction |
| `value` | any | no | Optional: only retract facts with this object value. A bare string is a literal; use {"iri": "..."} for a reference, or {"int"\|"float"\|"bool": ...}. With entity + predicate this pins a single triple. |

## `quipu_retract_episode`

Episode-scoped logical retraction: retract all currently-active facts an episode's ingest contributed (activity node, entities, edges, reified statements), via the bitemporal valid_to close path. Logical, not physical — time-travel history is preserved. Entities and other episodes' facts are untouched. Idempotent. Node IDENTITY is protected: by default (on_orphan=preserve) rdfs:label/rdf:type survive for any node that other episodes still reference, so retraction never leaves an unlabelled, untyped ghost. The response always reports identity_orphans.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is performing the retraction |
| `episode` | string | yes | Episode name/identifier to retract (aliases: episode_id, name) |
| `episode_id` | string | no | Alias for episode. |
| `name` | string | no | Alias for episode. |
| `on_orphan` | string: `preserve`, `refuse`, `allow` | no | What to do when retraction would strip rdfs:label/rdf:type from a node other episodes still reference. preserve (default): keep its identity alive. refuse: reject the whole retraction. allow: legacy strict scope — creates ghosts, reported in identity_orphans. |
| `orphan_policy` | string | no | Alias for on_orphan. |
| `timestamp` | string | no | ISO-8601 timestamp for the retraction |

## `quipu_retract_source`

RETRACT-ONLY repair: retract every currently-live fact whose transaction source equals an exact string. Reaches facts that no snapshot replacement can touch — quipu_knot composes its own tag as snapshot:<key>, so facts written under any other source (a free-form producer string, a hand-run CLI promote) were previously unretractable forever. There is NO turtle input: the transaction cannot carry an assertion, so this cannot write facts attributed to the named producer. The retraction is stamped with its OWN source, repair:<ticket>, never the source being cleared. PLANS BY DEFAULT: without apply=true it writes nothing and reports what would be retracted, so planned:0 means 'that source owns nothing live'. Applying requires expect=<planned> as a confirmation handshake, and the response reports 'remaining' — a fresh read of the post-state, not an echo of the request. RE-KEYING ORDER: retract FIRST, then re-promote canonically; asserting first is skipped as a duplicate and the retraction then removes everything.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | no | Who is performing the repair |
| `apply` | boolean | no | Default false = plan only, nothing is written. true commits the retraction and requires 'expect'. |
| `expect` | integer | no | Required with apply=true: the planned count you are confirming. A mismatch is refused — the store moved, or this is not the source you measured. |
| `graph` | string | no | Optional registered committed-graph IRI; absent targets ROOT. Same graph rules as quipu_knot. |
| `repair` | string | yes | Ticket or reason. Stamped on the retraction transaction as repair:&lt;ticket>, so the log records who cleared these facts and why. |
| `source` | string | yes | EXACT transaction source string to retract. Matched literally — never by prefix or pattern. Read it from GET /transactions or an entity's history. |
| `timestamp` | string | no | ISO-8601 timestamp for the retraction |

## `quipu_search`

Semantic vector search (default), opt-in SQLite FTS5 keyword search, or configurable lexical/vector hybrid fusion. Keyword mode requires query text and an enabled, backfilled index; it needs no embedding provider. Ranked REST results are diagnostic candidates; native MCP renders admitted context only. Agent context uses context_results when insufficient_context is false under quipu-context/v1.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all_graphs` | boolean | no | Search ROOT and all registered named graphs, excluding metadata and configured search.exclude_graphs. New stores default to ALL; existing stores retain ROOT until explicitly broadened. Configuration overrides the stored default. |
| `alpha` | number | no | Semantic weight. Hybrid alpha=1 preserves semantic results exactly, alpha=0 returns keyword results. |
| `anchor` | string | no | Root the search on ONE entity (IRI, CURIE or exact label; ambiguity is refused, never guessed) and rank by hop distance from it. Requires [quipu.search] anchored = true on the server. |
| `anchor_mode` | string: `decay`, `sort`, `filter` | no | decay (default): score x decay^hops; sort: hops first; filter: only reachable results. |
| `context_similarity_floor` | number | no | Raw cosine floor for context admission only; ranking is unchanged. Exact subject/identifier and term coverage are also required. |
| `decay` | number | no | Per-hop multiplier in (0, 1] for decay mode (default 0.5). |
| `direction` | string: `both`, `out`, `in` | no | Edge direction to traverse (default both). |
| `embedding` | array | no | Pre-computed query embedding vector (f32 array). Takes precedence over query. |
| `entity_type` | string | no | Optional: restrict to entities of this rdf:type IRI |
| `explain` | boolean | no | Return score components, matched lexical fields, applied filters and highlighted snippets; anchored search also returns a shortest path. |
| `filters` | object | no | Equivalent strict AST: {term:string}, {not:expr}, {and:[expr,expr]}, {or:[expr,expr]}. Mutually exclusive with structured_query. |
| `fusion` | string: `weighted`, `rrf` | no | Min-max score blend or weighted reciprocal rank fusion. |
| `graph` | string | no | Search one registered graph IRI, or all. Unknown IRIs are refused. Omitted scope uses the stored default (ALL for new stores, ROOT for existing stores), unless configuration overrides it. |
| `graphs` | array | no | Search the union of these registered graph IRIs. Mutually exclusive with graph/all_graphs. |
| `group_ids` | array | no | Optional: best-effort filter to entities from these provenance groups (episode-scoped label, NOT an isolation boundary; `/knot` facts are ungrouped and dropped from a group scope) |
| `infer_types` | boolean | no | Keyword mode only: type scope includes subclass inference when true; defaults false (asserted full-IRI types only). Type tokens are always asserted; response marks both choices. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum results (default: 10) |
| `max_hops` | integer | no | Anchor neighbourhood radius (default 3, server cap 4). |
| `mode` | string: `semantic`, `keyword`, `hybrid` | no | Keyword: literal terms and quoted phrases ranked by BM25 over labels, alt labels, descriptions/full bodies, literal attributes, type names and IRI local tokens. Requires [quipu.search] keyword=true. |
| `query` | string | no | Natural language search query (auto-embedded when EmbeddingProvider is attached) |
| `ranking` | string: `content`, `semantic` | no | Content ranking demotes repository artifacts lacking explanatory content; semantic returns raw cosine order. |
| `rrf_k` | number | no | Positive RRF constant; server default 60. |
| `structured_query` | string | no | Explicit boolean field/phrase/prefix candidate expression. Requires structured=true and SQLite. Candidate selection precedes ranking; default off. |
| `valid_at` | string | no | Point-in-time for temporal filtering (ISO-8601) |
| `verbose` | boolean | no | Return expanded full IRIs instead of default CURIE-compacted values. |
| `via` | array | no | Traverse only these predicate IRIs (replaces the default exclusions). |

## `quipu_set`

Atomically SET (entity, predicate) to exactly one value in the ROOT/default graph. Supplying a graph field is refused; named-graph facts are untouched. Retracts every current object on that predicate and asserts the new one in a single transaction. The supersede primitive — re-parenting (reports_to A -> B) is one call, with no empty-predicate window and no way to end up with two supervisors by forgetting the retract half. SINGLE-VALUE semantics: replaces ALL current objects; to add without removing, assert via quipu_knot.

| `source` | string | no | Provenance source of the update. |
| `timestamp` | string | no | ISO-8601 timestamp for the supersede |
| `value` | any | yes | New object value. A bare string is a literal; use {"iri": "..."} for an edge, or {"int"\|"float"\|"bool": ...} / {"value", "lang"\|"datatype"}. A bare string aimed at an IRI-valued predicate is refused loudly. |

| `since` | integer | no |  |

## `quipu_unified_search`

Unified knowledge search for Bobbin integration. Combines text and optional vector search, returning results tagged with source='knowledge' and normalized 0-1 scores. When an EmbeddingProvider is attached, the query is auto-embedded for semantic search.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `embedding` | array | no | Optional pre-computed query embedding. When omitted and EmbeddingProvider is attached, query is auto-embedded. |
| `expand_links` | boolean | no | Expand results via graph links (default: true) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum results (default: 10) |
| `max_facts_per_entity` | integer | no | Maximum facts per entity (default: 10) |
| `query` | string | yes | Natural language search query |

Time-travel query: see facts as they were at a given point

## `quipu_update`

Execute SPARQL 1.1 Update through the guarded update endpoint. Use explicit GRAPH clauses for named graphs; absent scope has standard SPARQL default-graph semantics. Actor/source are declared provenance, not authorization.

| `actor` | string | no |  |
| `source` | string | no |  |
| `update` | string | yes |  |

Validate RDF data against SHACL shapes without writing

| `data` | string | yes | RDF data in Turtle format to validate |

## `quipu_verdict_verify`

Verify a signed Verdict against the root of trust AS OF the signature (signing-plane S1): the signature must be valid under a key registered to the verifier at that instant, AND that same registration must authorize the predicate. 'trusted' is that conjunction — the property a consumer should gate on. Pass 'verdict' (the stored verdict's IRI) for a trust decision: quipu then reads when the store recorded the signature, which the signer cannot choose. 'as_of.basis' says which instant was used (recorded | caller-supplied | now). A caller-supplied signed_at/tx is a what-if: 'trusted' is then always false and the answer is in 'would_verify_as_of_supplied_instant'.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authenticator_data` | string | no | webauthn-* only: base64url authenticatorData from the assertion |
| `client_data_json` | string | no | webauthn-* only: base64url clientDataJSON from the assertion; its challenge must equal the one quipu derives from the verdict message |
| `evidence_hash` | string | yes | Evidence hash the signature seals |
| `outcome` | string | yes | Verdict outcome (satisfied \| unsatisfied \| unknown) |
| `predicate_id` | string | yes | Predicate the verdict attests |
| `scheme` | string | no | Signature scheme: ed25519 (default) \| webauthn-es256 \| webauthn-eddsa \| sshsig-sk-ed25519. Hardware schemes are refused unless [quipu.governance] hardware_verdict_schemes is on, and verify only against registrations declaring the same aegis:signatureScheme |
| `signature` | string | yes | The signature over the verdict message: hex for ed25519 (default); base64url DER/raw assertion signature for webauthn-*; the armored SSH SIGNATURE block for sshsig-sk-ed25519 |
| `signed_at` | string | no | Explicit valid-time instant to verify at (a what-if query; default now) |
| `target_ref` | string | yes | Target the verdict is about |
| `tier` | string | no | Evidence tier (default: committed) |
| `tx` | integer | no | Explicit transaction to verify as of (a what-if query; default latest) |
| `verdict` | string | no | IRI of the stored verdict carrying this signature; verify as of when the store recorded it (preferred for trust decisions) |
| `verifier` | string | yes | Verifier IRI whose registered key verifies the signature |

## `quipu_verifier_authorized`

Check the Phase-0 verifier registry: may this verifier attest this predicate? The discovery half of the governance gate — lets an agent learn who is authorized before trusting (or requesting) an attestation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `predicate` | string | yes | Predicate IRI to attest |
| `signed_at` | string | no | Valid-time instant to check at (default now) |
| `tx` | integer | no | Transaction to check as of (default latest) |
| `verifier` | string | yes | Verifier IRI |
